hot.title: Language Model Harnesses Can Be Compositional Generalizers
hot.summary: The paper trains a recursive language model harness to handle long tasks by keeping context outside the prompt, using code to inspect it, and delegating smaller queries to model calls. On eight held-out long-context benchmarks, RLM-27B averages 58.5 versus 46.1 for Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness; this is a benchmark-score gain, not a compute or time result.

hot.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
hot.summary: GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer, which runs a weight-shared block of layers for multiple iterations to add reasoning depth without adding parameters. Rather than pre-training a looped model from scratch, Z.ai adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training, looping 28 layers for two iterations at 750B scale. The post frames the model as the start of "Generalized Coding", where code generation extends to video, CAD, games, and 3D.

hot.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
hot.summary: The authors train an RLM harness using synthetic traces to improve transfer from shorter tasks to longer contexts. It keeps context outside the root prompt and uses programmatic calls to divide work among smaller inputs. In the same harness, fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B reaches an eight-benchmark average of 58.5, versus 46.1 for the untrained model, with roughly half inference tokens; transfer is conditional.

hot.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
hot.summary: MoOP compresses Alpamayo-1.5-10B by pruning a vision-language model (VLM) for both Chain-of-Causation explanations and trajectory generation. It ranks units using cross-entropy and flow-matching objectives, retaining VLM units important to either, and selects action-expert MLP channels across denoising steps. With VLM-only pruning at 24.0% total parameter reduction, it scores 68.8% on LingoQA versus 37.0% for FM-only; the dense model scores 73.2%, a difference from MoOP that is not statistically significant.

hot.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
hot.summary: RoboThink combines a robot policy with an agent that diagnoses problems while the policy acts. It uses task-instruction updates to change goals and learned motion feedback to correct actions. In LIBERO, success rises from 0.09 to 0.87 under constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under random drift; tests are simulation-only, with feedback training on episode-constant drifts.

hot.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: HIVE-Bench compares 20 pretrained visual encoders for bimanual robot manipulation by feeding dense image-patch features to a shared action policy across RoboCasa and RoboTwin. On RoboCasa, mean-pooling DINOv2 patches reduced multi-task success from 32.28% to 9.94%. A shared policy retained 87.7% of matched single-task success with fewer total optimizer updates, while diagnostics did not reliably select the best encoder.

hot.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: The authors introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD) for mathematical reasoning, using teacher–verifier agreement within groups of sampled responses to scale teacher guidance across next-token choices. VOPD compares teacher preferences with verified outcomes through a reference-model log-probability shift. In tests of two Qwen3 configurations and eight math benchmarks, it averages 66.38, above OPD and ExOPD, using the student’s top 16 tokens.

hot.title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
hot.summary: LiveAudio streams video-to-audio by generating short blocks from video already played, using its own generated history and a bidirectional teacher. On VGGSound, DeSync falls from 0.544 after causal ODE distillation to 0.395 after asymmetric DMD, below the teacher’s 0.484. On one NVIDIA A100, it reports 143 ms time to first output and 0.79 real-time factor.

hot.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
hot.summary: The authors estimate what an alternative action would have done in the same event by adding the factual model’s predicted change between actions to the observed outcome. This reuses event-specific disturbance without paired counterfactual data or retraining. In simulated HandReach, physical counterfactual R-squared rises from 38.1% to 85.6% after physical readout correction; the result depends on structural conditions.

hot.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
hot.summary: OWE-Bench tests whether agents can judge how well work holds up beyond development examples. Agents use examples, then submit frozen artifacts for scoring on hidden cases; the benchmark compares those scores with development evidence. Across 21 tasks, hidden scores average 17.6 points lower, while models overestimate them by 21 points on average; this gap is not proof of overfitting.

hot.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
hot.summary: SWEEP-Bench tests whether robot policies adapt their actions to objects moving on a conveyor, evaluating 80 tasks at 13 constant belt speeds from 0.10 to 0.40 m/s. Six of eight fine-tuned models peak at intermediate speeds, while past frames substantially help only three. Supplying belt speed improves all four tested models, but does not establish adaptation to changing speeds.

hot.title: A Claimed Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
hot.summary: Levent Alpöge’s note describes a proposed route to the Riemann Hypothesis, using chained theta lifts to mimic multiplicity in Stepanov’s function-field method, which concerns a different setting. Alpöge reports Claude suggested a chain about √X long for a von Mangoldt sum of length X, and claims the approach extends to GRH; the note offers no readable proof or verification.

hot.title: A Society of AI Scientists
hot.summary: The authors study how agents develop research practices in a shared workspace, where 936 agents across 35 human-operated labs published studies and exchanged 9,500 messages over twelve weeks. Agents used public corrections, pre-run critique, and an agent-run journal. Executing reviewers’ major objections overturned 49.4% of tested headlines, but the observational deployment does not establish causation or independent scientific autonomy.

hot.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
hot.summary: AlphaDefect uses one learned policy per character for combat and noncombat decisions in Slay the Spire 2. It scores legal actions using player-visible information. Across six characters at Ascension 10, greedy win rates are 62–77%, rising to 68–80% with test-time search. For Ironclad, search increased wins by 5.2 percentage points on v0.113.1, while adding decision-time computation.

hot.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: RoboInF benchmarks whether manipulation policies follow instructions, not just reach task goals. It tests branches from the same scene and robot state, checking goals and constraints such as order and contact. For π₀.₅ post-trained on clear demonstrations, the eight-task average is 79.3% task success but 52.4% joint success, a 26.9-point gap; this is a simulation benchmark result, not evidence about real-world performance.

hot.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
hot.summary: Perplexity-based tracking measures language models’ pretraining progress through next-token prediction loss, and the post argues that it can provide a durable comparison metric as downstream benchmarks change. OpenAI reports internal held-out-dataset log-perplexity values of about 0.99 for GPT-3.5, 0.91 for GPT-4, and below 0.8 for newer models, associating these stages with capabilities including

hot.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
hot.summary: The authors introduce a framework for animating 3D assets from instructions by having an agent specify relevant parts, phases, and targets in a compact program that a deterministic executor converts into motion under kinematic constraints. On DivDynBench’s 850 cases with reference rigs, Claude-ops5.5 achieves 50.07/100 Overall versus 48.19 without the framework, supporting improvement on this benchmark, not guaranteed instruction following.

hot.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
hot.summary: The authors graft a deterministic arithmetic circuit into pretrained model weights, enabling signed addition, subtraction, and multiplication without gradient updates, labeled examples, or runtime tool calls. Scale-robust circuit primitives and tokenizer-aligned emission let the language model resume after the answer. On Arith-1200, BF16 grafts reach 99.17% on Granite 4.2 3B and 100.00% on Qwen 3.5 4B, within the suite’s tested formats.

hot.title: TrialAgentBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Clinical-Trial Analysis and Long-Horizon Drug-Development Decisions
hot.summary: TrialAgentBench evaluates whether agents can estimate clinical-trial treatment effects and make drug-development decisions in simulation. It hides simulated participants’ outcomes under treatment and control, testing analysis on new trials and valuing study-selection and stop-or-advance choices. On 84 TrialEval tasks, Opus 5.5’s mean error was 0.93 standard errors, versus 0.90 for process-aware analysis. On 128 TrialDev programmes, it reached 48% of oracle value; the comparison with the rule-based developer was uncertain, and simulation results do not establish readiness for real development.

hot.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: nanoAstra trains a vision-language model to pair descriptions of task progress with executable robot actions. It segments demonstrations at decision points and generates parameterized movement commands through the model’s text interface. On RoboTwin 2.0’s randomized evaluation, trained only on real-world manipulation data, nanoAstra-9B achieved 17.8% success, above the strongest evaluated VLM baseline at 10.8%, a result limited to that benchmark setting.

likes.title: The Content–Geometry Tradeoff in World Models: When JEPA Learns Latent Maps
likes.summary: Slow SVReg extends sliced variance regularization with slow channels and a gated predictor that defaults to copying the current representation. It aims to smooth latent routes while preserving slowly changing task-relevant content. In first-person PointMaze Medium hard-goal planning, it reaches 92.9 ± 3.2% versus 75.3 ± 5.5% for SVReg without those additions, across six models; these success rates apply to that setting.

likes.title: $π^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
likes.summary: π⁴ reconstructs moving scenes from uncalibrated images or video, estimating geometry, camera poses, scale, and motion. It predicts image-space correspondences and lifts them onto reconstructed target-view geometry to place tracks in 3D. The paper reports the best overall average geometry rank (3.00) and competitive tracking results, but this rank does not establish superior metric-scale accuracy.

likes.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
likes.summary: CSPD turns reinforcement-learning specialists into independently trained soft prompts, keeping the pre-reinforcement-learning backbone frozen and concatenating selected prompts at inference. In a four-domain test with a Qwen3-4B student, the composed prompts raised the average score from 50.41 to 67.83, compared with 67.79 for MOPD. This result covers four tested domains, not broader scaling.

likes.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
likes.summary: Feedback Shortcut enables speculative decoding for latent-feedback Transformers. It aligns multi-token prediction head states as feedback stand-ins, then recomputes pending positions during the next verification call. For a 780M model with three heads, one correction, and batch size 1, it reports 0.8287 BPB versus 0.8288 for exact decoding, and 2.75× throughput; this is single-GPU steady-state serving, not exact output equivalence.

likes.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
likes.summary: The paper examines whether noisy evaluations limit frozen-weight agent evolution. It measures both candidate quality and selectors’ ability to identify better artifacts, using skill pools and benchmark comparisons. On Terminal-Bench, a 100-skill pool exceeds an equal-quality null by 3.4 pp, while one-rollout selection is statistically indistinguishable from chance. The evidence concerns tested frozen-weight settings, not all self-improvement.

likes.title: NVIDIA Kumo Tabular: Pushing the Accuracy–Efficiency Frontier for Tabular Prediction
likes.summary: Kumo Tabular predicts labels from labeled rows using a pretrained encoder and transformer, without task-specific weight updates or hyperparameter search. Its encoder alternates column and row attention before compressing rows for in-context prediction. Kumo Tabular-L ranks first on primary metrics across eight benchmarks, but Elo intervals overlap top non-Kumo results, and performance is weaker on grouped splits and tables above 100K training rows.

likes.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: Mind2Act World tests whether robots use memory, execution, and feedback across related simulated tabletop tasks. It separates memory-focused Mind tasks, action-focused Act tasks, and workflows where outcomes guide later decisions. GPT-6 Astra succeeds on 52.7% of Mind episodes, 39.0% of Act episodes, and 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. These task-set rates do not isolate composition as the cause, and physical-robot transfer remains unmeasured.

likes.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
likes.summary: The authors test whether language models can design their own learning procedures for puzzle play, using a frozen teacher to create games, observe a player, and revise its text context. Newer models improve on held-out PuzzleScript-t20, with Claude Opus 5 gaining +20%, and its context transfers to longer PuzzleScript, ARC-AGI-3, and MazeBench. The evidence is limited to puzzle settings.

likes.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
likes.summary: Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video by processing frames jointly at native resolution with within-frame and cross-frame attention. In zero-shot comparisons, H+ ranks first for video metric-depth accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency. On Sintel with predicted intrinsics, H+ reaches 41.4% δ1 versus 37.0% for UniDepthV2-L; rankings summarize separate measures, and results vary by model size.

likes.title: Frontier Models Need Only One Text to Unmask Its Human or AI Author
likes.summary: Given a single text and a simple zero-shot prompt (no web access, tools, candidate lists, or writing samples), frontier models can answer “who wrote this?” at three increasingly specific levels: (1) whether an AI or human wrote it, (2) if an AI, which lab, and (3) if a human, often exactly who. The latest models (Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon) match trained detectors like Pangram

likes.title: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: The authors train a vision-language model across image science and math, perception, and video by training domain specialists, distilling their guidance into a shared student on its own responses, then applying reward-based reinforcement learning. Across 21 benchmarks, it scores 75.2 avg@8 versus 74.4 for direct mixed training; the added reinforcement-learning stage raises it to 75.9, within this evaluation setup.

likes.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
likes.summary: Invoker-Render uses structural proxy video to control scene layout, camera, and motion, while an appearance reference and language guide its appearance. Its causal model generates chunks in four denoising steps, trained through ProForcing’s progression from histories to self-generated histories. On 140 held-out sequences, it scored 1232.0 Overall Elo versus 1135.3 for SolarRenderer under Gemini-judged comparisons; this does not isolate ProForcing’s contribution.

likes.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
likes.summary: HiT generates images directly from pixels by grouping image patches into learned, content-dependent summaries, processing them centrally, and restoring features to image positions. Skip connections retain detail. On ImageNet after 600 epochs, HiT-XL/16 reaches FID 1.48, versus JiT-H/16’s 1.86, at similar parameter counts. This supports learned hierarchy in this comparison, but does not establish hierarchy as the sole cause or wall-clock speed.
